posts.summary: Two English floors six hundred years apart, made the same way. Rosa y Granada is Catherine of Aragon's rose and pomegranate as a medieval inlaid tile, white slip in red clay under lead. Encaustic is the Victorian revival for Pugin's churches and the Palace of Westminster: four clays, no glaze, lions and lettering. Both share one material file with two recipes, and both are cousins of the Barcelona cement tile.
posts.title: Clay in Clay
